transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

My doctors keep telling me I’m too thin and need to eat more, but I honestly don’t see what the fuss is about. I feel like I’m just being careful with my health and staying disciplined, so I'm a bit confused as to why they insisted I come here.
Do you think your weight is normal, and is there a specific weight or body shape that you're trying to achieve?

I think my weight is perfectly fine, and I’m actually pleased when the scale goes down because being lean feels like a sign of good discipline. When I look in the mirror, I don't see "too thin" at all; I just see soft spots around my belly that I'd still like to trim down to keep my heart healthy. To me, keeping the weight off is just the sensible way to stay healthy.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you ever see yourself as overweight even when others might say you're underweight?

I wouldn't say I look obese, but when I look in the mirror, I certainly don't see the "dangerously thin" person the doctors describe. I mostly just see spots around my stomach that still look a bit soft, and I honestly think I could stand to trim that down a bit more to keep my heart in good shape. To me, keeping those areas lean just seems like sensible discipline rather than a problem.
Do you restrict your food intake or exercise excessively in order to achieve this lean body shape you're aiming for, and if so, does it feel like it's taking up a lot of your time or energy?

I do eat very lightly, usually just sharing a small bowl of oatmeal in the morning and picking at some vegetables or half an apple later, which I think is plenty for an older man. I don't exercise excessively, just my senior walking club, so I wouldn't say it takes up too much of my time or thoughts. However, I have been feeling quite physically drained lately and lacking the energy to keep up with chores and my wife's medical appointments.
Can you help me understand why you think your current eating habits and weight are healthy, despite your doctors' concerns, and how you balance this with feeling physically drained?

To me, staying thin and eating light feels like the only sensible, disciplined way to protect my heart, especially after watching several of my buddies suffer from heart attacks. It’s true that I’ve been feeling physically drained lately and struggling to keep up with my wife’s appointments and household chores, but I still view this strict control as absolutely necessary for my health. Compared to the alternative, keeping the weight off just seems like the right thing to do.
Do you think your perception of your body weight and shape might be different from how others see you, and if so, how does that make you feel?

Yes, my doctors and friends constantly tell me I'm too thin, which is frustrating because I don't see what they see at all. When I look in the mirror, I just notice soft spots on my belly that I feel I still need to trim down to protect my heart. To me, staying lean is just a sign of healthy discipline and control, so all this fuss is very confusing.
Do you believe that if you were to gain a small amount of weight, it would lead to serious health problems, such as a heart attack, and is that fear driving your desire to stay lean?

Yes, that is exactly what I fear. When I even think about gaining weight or eating things like butter on my toast, I get a tight feeling in my chest and picture my arteries clogging up. After watching my close friends suffer from heart attacks, staying lean feels like the only sensible, disciplined way to protect my heart.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happens or what you experience when you think about gaining weight, such as any physical sensations or emotions that come up for you?

If I even imagine putting butter on my toast or having ice cream with my grandkids, I get this tight feeling in my chest and feel incredibly anxious. I immediately picture my arteries clogging up and my belly popping out, which absolutely terrifies me. Because of that anxiety, I just stick strictly to my "safe" foods to keep those thoughts away.

Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight and its health consequences if you were at a weight that others considered healthy, or is your fear specifically tied to how you perceive your own body shape and weight?

I believe both aspects play a big role in my fear. Even if others call a higher weight "healthy," the thought of gaining weight makes me panic about my heart failing and my arteries clogging up. At the same time, when I look in the mirror, I still see soft areas around my belly that I feel need to be trimmed down, so my fear is tied to both my health anxieties and how I perceive my body shape.
Can you describe a situation where you would feel comfortable and not anxious about your weight, even if it meant not being as lean as you are now?

To be honest, I cannot picture any situation where I would feel comfortable being less lean than I am now. Even just imagining eating normal foods or gaining weight triggers intense anxiety, a tight feeling in my chest, and vivid fears of clogged arteries. Staying thin feels like the only safe, disciplined way I have to protect my health and my heart.
When you experience anxiety about gaining weight, is it primarily because you fear the health consequences or because you are distressed by the idea of your body changing shape or appearance?

It is actually a combination of both. Imagining weight gain makes me worry about health consequences like my arteries clogging up, but I also struggle with my appearance and hate the thought of my belly looking soft or popping out when I want to keep it trimmed and disciplined.
When you think about gaining weight, is your anxiety more about how your body would look, or is it solely about the potential health risks you associate with weight gain?

It is really a mix of both. I worry deeply about my heart and picture my arteries clogging up if I eat richer foods, but I also get anxious about my appearance and worry about my belly looking soft or popping out if I gain weight.
When you think about your body shape and weight, is your desire to stay lean more driven by a fear of looking a certain way or a fear of the health problems you believe will come with weight gain?

My desire to stay lean is primarily driven by the fear of health problems, specifically clogging my arteries or having a heart attack like my friends from the walking club did. However, I also really dislike looking soft in the belly and want to avoid that. Ultimately, keeping my weight down feels like the only sensible, disciplined way to protect my heart.
When you're anxious about your weight, is the fear of looking unhealthy or the fear of actually being unhealthy more prominent in your thoughts?

It is definitely the fear of actually being unhealthy, particularly regarding my heart and arteries, that dominates my thoughts. Looking thin doesn't seem unhealthy to me at all; rather, I see it as a sign of discipline and good health. When I think about gaining weight, I picture clogged arteries and heart attacks, which is what truly scares me after seeing what my friends have gone through.

Can you rate on a scale of 1 to 10 how much your fear of weight gain is driven by concerns about your appearance versus concerns about your health, with 1 being entirely about appearance and 10 being entirely about health?

I would rate it about an 8 or 9 out of 10, as my main driver is almost entirely about protecting my health, keeping my heart in good shape, and preventing my arteries from clogging after watching my friends suffer from heart disease. The remaining point or two is just that I dislike seeing my belly look soft or popping out, but even that is ultimately tied back to keeping my heart healthy. Keeping trim just feels like the sensible thing to do.

Can you clarify if your restrictive eating habits and excessive exercise, if present, are primarily aimed at preventing the perceived health risks associated with weight gain, or if they are also significantly driven by a desire to achieve a specific body shape or appearance?

For me, both of those aspects are closely connected. My primary goal is to protect my heart and prevent clogged arteries, especially after my doctor's warnings and seeing my friends suffer from heart disease. However, when I look in the mirror, I still see areas like my belly looking soft and feel I need to trim that down further to stay in good shape.

If you were assured by medical professionals that your current weight and eating habits were not healthy and were causing you physical harm, would you still feel compelled to maintain your current weight and eating habits due to your concerns about body shape and appearance?

My doctors have actually been telling me exactly that, but it is incredibly hard for me to change my habits. When I look in the mirror, I don't see someone who is too thin; I just see areas, like my belly, that still look soft and need trimming. The thought of gaining weight or seeing my belly pop out makes me feel so anxious and tight in my chest that I would still feel a strong, compelling need to maintain my disciplined eating to feel in control and protect my heart.

Can you describe how your fear of weight gain and its health consequences would change if you were medically assured that your current weight is unhealthy and causing harm, versus if you were at a weight considered healthy by others but still perceived yourself as overweight?

My doctors are already telling me my weight is dangerously low, but it is hard to accept because being thin feels like the only way to protect my heart. If I were to gain weight to what others call "healthy," I would feel immense anxiety and chest tightness, constantly worrying about clogged arteries and seeing myself as soft or overweight. That scenario feels much more threatening to me than my current state.

Do you think your fear of gaining weight and its associated health risks would decrease if you were able to achieve a body shape or weight that you perceive as ideal, or would your fear persist regardless of your actual weight or body shape?

I believe the worry would persist because it feels like there is always more to trim. Even though I've already lost weight, I still see soft spots on my belly in the mirror that I feel I need to work on to protect my heart. The fear of clogging my arteries or having my belly pop out is so immediate that I feel I must always stay disciplined and stick to my safe foods.

If you were to gain weight to a point where your doctors and others considered you healthy, but you still perceived yourself as overweight, would your fear of health consequences like heart disease decrease, or would it remain the same due to your body image concerns?

My fear of heart disease would actually remain very high, or even get worse, because in my mind seeing myself as "soft" is directly tied to the image of clogged arteries and heart strain. Even if doctors told me I was at a healthy weight, if I looked in the mirror and saw soft spots, I wouldn't be able to shake the feeling that my heart is in danger. That is why I feel I absolutely must keep tight control over my body shape.

If you were somehow magically able to completely eliminate your concerns about your body shape and appearance, would you still feel the need to restrict your food intake and maintain your current weight due to health concerns?

Yes, I would absolutely still feel the need to restrict my food. My primary motivation has always been about protecting my heart, especially after my past cholesterol warnings and seeing my friends from the walking club suffer from heart disease. Even without any concerns about my appearance, the fear of clogged arteries would make me feel that eating light is the only responsible way to stay healthy.

If a medical test could conclusively prove that your current weight and eating habits are not causing the health problems you fear, such as clogged arteries, would this change your desire to maintain your current weight and eating habits?

I'm really not sure how I would react to that, as it's not a scenario I've ever thought about. Even if a test showed that, I think I would still hesitate to change because losing control of my eating and seeing my belly get soft just feels so dangerous for my heart. It is very hard to imagine letting go of that discipline.

If you were to experience significant health complications directly resulting from your restrictive eating habits, such as severe malnutrition or organ damage, would your desire to maintain your current weight and body shape outweigh your concerns about these immediate health risks?

I'm a bit confused by that question, because I really don't believe my disciplined eating is putting me in any danger of malnutrition or organ damage. In my mind, staying lean is the only way to protect my heart and avoid the terrible heart complications I've seen my friends suffer from. The threat of clogging my arteries and gaining weight feels like a much more real and immediate danger to me than any risk of being "too thin."

If you were certain that your heart health was not at risk from gaining a small amount of weight, would you still feel compelled to maintain your current restrictive eating habits due to concerns about your body shape and appearance?

Yes, even if heart health weren't an issue at all, I would still feel highly uncomfortable with the idea of gaining weight. When I look in the mirror, I still see areas like my belly looking soft or flabby, and the thought of it popping out really bothers me. Keeping control over my shape and avoiding that soft look brings a sense of discipline that is very hard for me to let go of, regardless of medical advice.
Can you imagine any scenario where your concerns about heart health and body shape would not dictate your eating habits, or would these concerns always influence your food choices?

It is very difficult for me to imagine any scenario where these concerns do not dictate my eating, as they feel constant and always influence my food choices. Even the thought of straying from my "safe" foods—like having butter on toast or ice cream with my grandkids—instantly triggers anxiety, a tight feeling in my chest, and mental images of clogged arteries or a soft belly. Because of this, these health and shape concerns always guide what I put on my plate.
Do you think your concerns about body shape and appearance are more prominent than your concerns about health risks when making decisions about your eating habits and weight?

For me, body shape and health risks are completely tied together rather than being two separate things. When I worry about my belly looking soft or putting on weight, I immediately associate it with clogged arteries and heart disease. My focus on staying lean is really about discipline and protecting my heart, not vanity.

If you were to experience a significant improvement in your overall health, such as normalized heart function and no signs of malnutrition, but still perceived yourself as being slightly overweight, would your desire to restrict your food intake decrease?

No, I don't think my desire to restrict would decrease at all. Even if my heart and nutrition were medically perfect, seeing any softness in the mirror makes me feel like I still need to trim down. The fear of my belly popping out and losing control of my weight would make it very hard to stop restricting and would keep me sticking to my safe foods.
Would you say that your fear of gaining weight is more about the potential health risks, such as heart disease, or is it equally or more about how your body would look if you gained weight?

It is really a combination of both. I have an intense fear of my arteries clogging up and suffering from heart disease, especially after seeing my close friends go through it. But I also worry about how my body looks, specifically feeling anxious about my belly looking soft or popping out if I were to gain weight.
If you could achieve a body shape that you consider ideal, would your fear of health consequences like heart disease decrease, or would it remain the same?
I'm not really sure, as I haven't really thought about it that way. I think I would still worry, so I just focus on doing what I can day by day to keep my heart safe and stay disciplined.
If you were to gain weight but your body shape remained lean due to muscle tone or other factors, would your fear of health consequences like heart disease still be as prominent?

I'm not really sure, as I haven't really thought about it that way. To me, gaining weight and eating more always feels like it would immediately lead to clogged arteries and a softer belly, making it very hard to imagine staying lean.
